components.name: Kafka
components.quote: Loki can optionally use Apache Kafka, or a Kafka-protocol-compatible system, as a durable buffer on the write path.

components.name: client
components.quote: The query frontend merges the individual results into a final result and return it to the client.

components.name: distributor
components.quote: The distributor receives an HTTP POST request with streams and log lines.

components.name: ingester
components.quote: The ingester receives the stream with log lines and creates a chunk or appends to an existing chunk for the stream's data.

components.name: object storage
components.quote: Loki stores all data in a single object storage backend, such as Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3), Google Cloud Storage (GCS), Azure Blob Storage, among others.

components.name: querier
components.quote: The querier pulls sub-queries from the scheduler.

components.name: query frontend
components.quote: The query frontend receives an HTTP GET request with a LogQL query.

components.name: query scheduler
components.quote: passes them to the query scheduler

relations.quote: the distributor writes log streams as Kafka records to a configured topic
The distributor sends each stream to the appropriate ingester and its replicas (based on the configured replication factor).
Each ingester consumes from exactly one Kafka partition, determined by its position in the partition ring.
The querier passes the query to all ingesters for in-memory data.
The querier lazily loads data from the backing store and runs the query against it if ingesters returned no or insufficient data.
The querier pulls sub-queries from the scheduler.
The query frontend merges the individual results into a final result and return it to the client.
The query frontend splits the query into sub-queries and passes them to the query scheduler.
